title: SF2126 (2023-2024 Regular): Permit to carry application and renewal process modification

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction, 2023-02-21; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2023/0/SF/2126/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version as filed, 2023-02-21; no vote recorded. No struck text in the file, so which words of subd. 3 are new cannot be told from the text.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 3): (e) Applications for new permits must be submitted in person. Applications for permit renewals may be submitted in person, electronically, or by United States mail. If the applicant does not appear in person, the applicant's signature must be notarized. A sheriff may not require an applicant to make an appointment to submit an application.
Section 2: (b) Notwithstanding Minnesota Statutes, section 624.714, during a peacetime public health emergency a sheriff may require a person applying for or renewing a permit to carry in person to make an appointment to submit the application packet if the sheriff determines that this is warranted to prevent or reduce the spread of COVID-19 and the sheriff is requiring appointments for other similar matters. If a sheriff requires an appointment under this paragraph, the sheriff shall ensure that one is available within 30 days of the date that the applicant contacts the sheriff to make the appointment.
